doc.title: Jerry Dodgion interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, March 9, 1996

chapter: Early years and arriving in New York
title: Pop music of his youth and starting with professional bands
summary: Dodgion recalls radio bands and singers in the late 40s and early 50s and playing with professionals around San Francisco while in high school.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Growing up with radio, records and family listening

blocks.x: Can you tell me, what was pop music, what was the pop music of the time when you were first starting on your instrument, and did it influence where you went as a musician at all?

Gee, I don’t know. Pop music, like I remember it was just radio, you know just bands and singers and that was in the late 40s and early 50s. But when I got interested in it there was in school, and I just got lucky. I started working with professional musicians when I was in high school and I worked with some local bands around San Francisco that were great and very encouraging. The pop music, I didn’t find out until — I just really wasn’t too interested in the real, hard core pop, I mean that was like—
It was the era of, I guess the big band era had kind of ended.
